notes.claim: As the second point moves toward the first, the secant line's slope becomes a better approximation to the rate of change of the function at that point.
Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocity over a small time interval.
The instantaneous rate of change of a function is its derivative, the rate of change at any point along the function.
dy/dx is written from the limit of the difference in y-values divided by the difference in x-values; the MCA syllabus likewise defines dy/dx as the limiting value of δy/δx.
Textbooks build the derivative as a limit of secants, while one teacher argues students should not base the derivative on the tangent's slope.
notes.contested: OpenStax's calculus text recognises the tangent as the limit of secant lines, whereas Bressoud (MAA) argues students should not base their understanding of the derivative on the slope of the tangent.

notes.claim: For i2: at a sharp corner a function has no derivative, because the slopes from the left and from the right settle on different values (OpenStax's example is f(x) = |x| at 0).
